A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the ribosomes of Escherichia coli are capable of binding aminoacyl tRNA, GTP, and factor G to form a functional ribosome complex which is capable of catalyzing the translocation of peptidyl tRNA from the A site to the P site.

The main takeaway from our work is that
antibiotics can be used to study the mechanism of protein synthesis and that they can be used to probe the relationship between the steps of protein biosynthetic processes.
the antibiotics we have studied are not simple inhibitors of translocation, but rather are complex inhibitors of the translocation reaction.
the ribosomes are not only the site of peptide synthesis, they also play a role in the translocation of the growing peptide chain.
